name: str_match
title: Extract components (capturing groups) from a match

origin.description: Extract the first match and its capturing groups. Unnamed groups are (pattern) and named groups are (?<name>pattern).

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A regular expression. Unlike the other stringr search functions, fixed, coll, boundary, and the empty string are errors. The pattern should contain at least one capturing group.

origin.details: Recycling and names follow the other stringr search functions. The first column is the complete match. Later columns are the capturing groups, in order. A group that did not participate is missing, as is a string that did not match. Named groups name the columns when pattern is a single pattern. The first column name is empty. A non-capturing group, (?:pattern), is not a column.
origin.value: A character matrix with one row for each element of string or pattern. Column 1 is the whole match, then one column for each capture group.

translation.description: Extract the first match and its capturing groups. Unnamed groups are (pattern) and named groups are (?<name>pattern).

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A plain string, list, or regex() pattern. fixed, coll, boundary, and the empty string raise ValueError. The message is that pattern must be a regular expression.

translation.details: check_lengths raises RecycleError when lengths other than 0 and 1 disagree. pattern_type must be regex. The call is stri_match_first_regex with pattern_opts. Column 0 is the whole match. A group that did not participate is NA. Named groups are stored on colnames when pattern is a single pattern, and the first name is empty. Patterns of different widths are padded with NA to the widest pattern.
translation.value: A list of rows. Each row is the match and its groups. A missing cell is stringi._na.NA, which is JSON null. colnames and ncol describe the matrix, including a matrix with no rows.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringr.match import str_match
x = ["<a> <b>", "<a> <>", "<a>", "", NA]
print(str_match(x, "<(.*?)> <(.*?)>"))
